chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi, from al-Amriki ibn Ali al-Khorasani, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot to enter into the state of Ihram for Hajj, and then remembered it while he was at Arafat. What is his status? He said: 'He says: O Allah, according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, so his Ihram is complete.' If he was unaware of how to enter Ihram—from the Day of Tarwiyah for Hajj until he returned to his country—and he performed all its rituals, then his Hajj is complete.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامَ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.بِعَرَفَاتٍ: At Arafat, the central station of Hajj
key_terms.مَنَاسِكَهُ: The rituals and rites of Hajj
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgot to enter Ihram until reaching Arafat?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who neglected the formal declaration of Ihram until reaching Arafat, establishing that reciting a specific formula invoking the Quran and Sunnah suffices to validate the state. It further distinguishes between mere forgetfulness at Arafat and total ignorance from the Day of Tarwiyah, where performing all rituals still renders the Hajj valid, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in cases of genuine oversight. This highlights the juristic flexibility within the Imami school regarding the timing and formality of Ihram initiation.
